To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the MPO-ANCA pattern is the most frequent ANCA specificity in the studied population of patients with vasculitides and isolated or predominant kidney involvement.
the anti-MPO antibodies in patients with ANCA-associated vasculitis are associated with a higher frequency of renal disease and lower frequency of glomerulonephritis.
anti-PR3 and MPO ANCA are associated with different clinical manifestations of systemic vasculitis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the role of the MPO-antibody in the pathogenesis of the vasculitis and the kidney involvement.
the study of the role of the immune system in the pathogenesis of the disease and the identification of the autoantibodies associated with the different forms of the disease.
the study of the role of anti-MPO antibodies in vasculitides and in other autoimmune disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of p-ANCA in the absence of anti MPO specificity should not lead to the diagnosis of a Wegener granulomatosis.

ANCA are a group of heterogeneous antibodies directed against a group of antigens of unknown structure and function, that are present in a wide variety of diseases and that have a role in the pathogenesis of the disease.
ANCA is not a disease, but a serological finding, which can be present in several diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of ANCA in patients with vasulitis and/or renal involvement, especially when they are positive for MPO, are associated with a better prognosis, as compared to the ANCA-negative group.
anti-MPO antibodies were detected in 41% of patients with vasculitic disease, but also in patients with other diseases.
anti-MPO antibodies were present in 41% of patients with vasculitides.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of anti-MPO antibodies is a strong predictor of poor outcome in AAV, and that it is associated with a higher incidence of renal involvement, and more severe renal disease.
the MPO-ANCA pattern is not specific for Wegener's disease and is not a good marker of renal involvement.
